name: Magellan
intro: Magellan used radar to see through Venus’s thick clouds and mapped 98% of its surface. In October 1994 it was steered deep into the atmosphere to study it, and it burned up. If any pieces reached the ground, nobody knows where, so this model floats above Venus’s clouds as a memorial.
status: Burned up in Venus’s sky in 1994
whyLeft: Its mapping was done and its power was dropping, so NASA used its last days for one more experiment: a dive into Venus’s thick air, where it broke apart and burned.
repurpose: Nothing is left to fix. Its ending was itself a reuse: the final dive turned the whole spacecraft into an instrument for measuring the atmosphere.

hotspots.title: Seeing through clouds
hotspots.text: Venus is always covered in clouds, so Magellan bounced radar off the ground, like seeing with echoes. Its map shows volcanoes, lava plains and craters across 98% of the planet.

photo.alt: Globe of Venus in orange tones made from radar data, showing bright highlands.
photo.caption: Venus without its clouds, made from Magellan’s radar maps. The colours are added; radar does not see colour.
photo.licenseEvidence: Commons page licence: “Public domain” (PD NASA); original source: from Planetary Photojournal.

hotspots.title: The windmill trick
hotspots.text: In its last weeks, Magellan turned its solar panels like windmill blades as it skimmed the air, so scientists could measure the drag. Then it sank deeper and burned up.

hotspots.title: Launched by a shuttle
hotspots.text: In 1989 Magellan became the first planetary explorer launched from a Space Shuttle. Astronauts on Atlantis released it from the cargo bay.

photo.alt: A spacecraft with a rocket stage rising out of the Space Shuttle’s cargo bay above Earth.
photo.caption: Magellan and its rocket stage leaving Space Shuttle Atlantis’s cargo bay on 4 May 1989.
photo.licenseEvidence: Commons page licence: “Public domain” (PD NASA); original source: https://images.nasa.gov/details-s30-71-052 (image link).

hotspots.title: Built from spares
hotspots.text: Magellan was partly built from spare parts left over from other missions. Its big dish antenna was a spare from Voyager.

hotspots.title: Braking with air
hotspots.text: In 1993 Magellan dipped into the top of Venus’s atmosphere again and again to shrink its orbit, the first planetary spacecraft to brake this way. Mars orbiters use the trick today.

funFact: Venus’s surface is hot enough to melt lead, so any piece of Magellan that reached the ground would have landed in an oven.
